title: Decomposing multi-agent collusion detection: a Schelling-coordination probe in a 2-agent open-model game

original_idea.body:
# Decomposing multi-agent collusion detection: a Schelling-coordination probe in a 2-agent open-model game

**Problem:** Agentic/multi-agent safety worries about emergent collusion. A scoped sub-problem from evaluations: in a simple two-agent coordination (Schelling) game between two instances of a small open model, do the agents coordinate above chance, and can a text-level monitor detect implicit coordination signals?

**Direction:** Decompose 'detect multi-agent collusion' into a measurable Schelling-game experiment. Set up two open-model agents that benefit from secretly coordinating on a hidden choice without explicit communication. Measure coordination rate vs a no-communication baseline, and test whether a monitor reading their visible messages can predict when collusion succeeds.

**Why it matters:** Model-organism-style study of coordination/collusion — explicitly favored — scoped to a 30h slice with open models and one GPU, no training. Multi-agent collusion is a medium-horizon, lab-deprioritized risk. Coordination-above-chance and monitor-detectability are clean deliverables.

**Relevant context:** Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI (2502.14143); agentic_safety governance-of-multi-agent open problem; Schelling-point coordination literature; cheap two-agent harness with open chat models.
